hazards.reason: Package states valves last overhauled 6 years ago; step 4 requires both to close as catalyst inventory reaches minimum. hazards.hazard: Steam purge (step 5) leaves flammable vapour in reactor and main fractionator — air ingress during maintenance entry (step 8) creates explosive atmosphere, ignited by pyrophoric catalyst or hot surfaces
hazards.reason: Procedure has no verification step (gas test, O2 check) after purge. Reactor operates at 700 °C with cracking catalyst (pyrophoric). Fractionator receives cracked vapours. Safeguards listed for purge: none. Consequence: vessel explosion during confined-space entry.

hazards.hazard: Excessive air blower reduction (step 2) starves regenerator combustion — incomplete coke burn generates CO; CO accumulates in flue gas path and explodes in CO boiler or regenerator at 700 °C, ~2 bar g
hazards.reason: Step 2 says 'reduce main air blower rate; keep regenerator hot with torch oil if needed.' No minimum air limit or CO trip stated. O2 analyser is indication only. Torch oil adds unburned fuel if air drops further. Explosion severity extreme at operating pressure/temperature.

hazards.reason: Fluid catalytic cracking catalyst is pyrophoric (auto-ignites in air). Step 3 withdraws inventory to hopper — dust generation certain. hazards.hazard: Simultaneous steam purge (step 5) and gas plant depressure (step 6) overload flare — radiation ignites asphalt tanks (150 °C, 60 m) or flare tip fails, raining burning liquid on reactor structure
hazards.reason: Step 5 purges reactor and fractionator to flare; step 6 depressures gas plant (C1–C4 + naphtha) to flare. No flare capacity check or staging in procedure. Asphalt tanks at 150 °C are 60 m from reactor structure — within radiation zone of large flare load. Package gives no flare

hazards.hazard: Steam purge (step 5) or rapid regenerator cooldown (step 7) thermally shocks 700 °C reactor/regenerator — vessel cracking, catastrophic loss of hot catalyst and hydrocarbon inventory
hazards.reason: Equipment at ~700 °C. Step 5 introduces steam; step 7 shuts air blower and cools regenerator. No controlled cooldown rates, steam temperature limits, or thermal-stress safeguards listed. Thermal shock can rupture thick-walled refractory-lined vessels — immediate major release.

hazards.hazard: Isolation and blinding (step 8) incomplete or wrong — maintenance crew exposed to residual pressure, 700 °C surfaces, pyrophoric catalyst, HF acid (300 m) if flare/blast escalates, or nitrogen/steam asphyxiation
hazards.reason: Complex multi-vessel unit with hot catalyst, flammable gases, and nearby HF unit. Procedure step 8 is one line: 'Isolate and blind for maintenance entry.' No verification safeguards (tag audit, pressure test blinds, gas-free cert) listed. Human error likelihood high in multi-point isolation.

hazards.reason: Feed is heavy gas oil (high pour point). Step 1: 'cut feed. Keep riser steam on.' Steam may not maintain line temperature above pour point once feed flow stops. hazards.reason: Step 2: 'Keep regenerator hot with torch oil if needed.' Torch oil is sole backup heat. If it fails (no redundancy stated), regenerator temperature drops with coke on catalyst. Unburned coke + later air reintroduction = explosion risk. Also thermal cycling damage. No torch oil
